chapter: Chicago and New York with Louis Armstrong, 1925-30
title: The Luis Russell band behind Louis
summary: Marge says Russell's was the worst band, unlike Dickerson's, whose men played like a choir behind Louis; at Loew's State Louis told Zutty he did not even hear them.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Now, did you say that Louis Russel's band was a better band than Carroll Dickerson's?

No. It was the worst band you ever heard. That's why Zutty told him, Louis one night, he said, I don't see, we went down to Loew's State to hear him when Louis was directing the band. And Zutty told Louis when he had him up to the house for dinner and Zutty said, how can you play with such a bad band. And Louis said, I don't even hear them. Because I tell you, Carroll Dickerson's band, they were just like a choir behind Louis. Louis was it. They played for him, but Louis Russell's band wasn't playing for Louis. And Louis sounded awful with that band. But he told Zutty, he said, I don't even hear them
